heroMetrics.label: Purchases · last 7 days

delta.text: orders up 5.4%, revenue down 19.9% — smaller average order after the sale window closed

heroMetrics.note: Sept 6-12 against Aug 30-Sep 5. Order count held and slightly improved; revenue fell because the LABORDAY26 sale (20% off sitewide, Sept 5-7) pulled a large, discounted day into the prior window. Sept 5 alone carried 21 orders and $1,704. This is a sale-timing effect, not a demand collapse.

heroMetrics.label: Add-to-cart · last 7 days

delta.text: down 21.8% — tracks the end of the sale window

heroMetrics.note: Add-to-cart is Humarian's intentional conversion proxy, reported alongside purchase because purchase attribution is severed at the Shopify checkout hop. The decline mirrors the sale ending: Sept 5 carried 124 add-to-carts on its own, against a normal run rate closer to 10-40 a day.

heroMetrics.label: Meta Ads · last 20 days

delta.text: delivery is steady at roughly $20-35/day; a Smile Guard advertorial ad set went live Sept 8

heroMetrics.note: Meta delivery is healthy and consistent. IMPORTANT MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: Meta's own Purchase event is currently registering zero. Website purchases, purchase conversion value and omni purchases all return null for every day Aug 25 through Sept 13 while impressions and spend run normally. Meta-side ROAS is therefore unreadable right now and is being worked as an open fault, not reported as ad failure.
heroMetrics.source: Meta Ads via Supermetrics · act_337218486645475 · Aug 25-Sep 13, pulled Sept 13, 2026

heroMetrics.label: Google Ads · last 20 days

delta.text: target cost per conversion raised $5 to $8 on Sept 13 to unlock delivery

heroMetrics.note: Branded search was under-spending against a $17/day budget. Diagnosis: zero percent of impressions were lost to budget on every single day, while 41-77% were lost to ad rank. The $5 target cost per conversion was throttling bids, not the budget. Target raised to $8 and verified live. A rebuilt non-branded pet symptom campaign also went live Sept 13 at $10/day.
heroMetrics.source: Google Ads 4875571866 via Supermetrics · Aug 25-Sep 13, pulled Sept 13, 2026

projectCards.name: Paid Ads — Google
projectCards.status: Rebuilt this week. The non-branded Women's Probiotic campaign was diagnosed and rebuilt: it had spent $147 for zero conversions because two of its keywords have zero monthly search volume, so Google's close-variant matching filled the gap with competitor brand names and vaginal-health queries the product does not serve. Rebuilt as exact-match digestive keywords with 82 negatives and a new ad, held paused. A pet symptom campaign (cat and dog vomiting/diarrhea, 23-50 cents a click against the $3.98 previously paid) went live Sept 13 at $10/day with a $150-or-30-day kill rule.

thisWeeksMove.label: Google Ads was rebuilt on evidence, and the measurement bugs got named
thisWeeksMove.body: Two things moved. The non-branded Google campaign that had burned $147 for nothing was diagnosed down to the root cause, two keywords with literally zero monthly search volume, and rebuilt; a much cheaper pet symptom campaign went live in its place with a spending kill rule agreed in advance. Separately, the GA4 double-count was fixed and Meta's Purchase event was caught returning zero, which means the numbers on this page are now either verified or explicitly flagged as unverifiable, with nothing in between.
thisWeeksMove.cta: Watch pet campaign orders in Shopify, and the Meta Events Manager check

lumenDid: Sept 13: Diagnosed why the non-branded Google campaign produced zero conversions on $147. Two of its keywords have zero monthly search volume, so Google matched them to competitor brand names and vaginal-health searches instead. Rebuilt it on exact-match digestive keywords with 82 negative keywords and a new ad that leads with bloating rather than feminine wellness.

Sept 13: Built and launched a pet symptom campaign (cat vomiting, dog diarrhea and related) at $10/day. These searches cost 23 to 50 cents against the $3.98 a click the old campaign was paying, and Humarian already ranks page one for the pet vomiting terms.

Sept 13: Found and fixed the cause of Google Ads under-spending. Zero percent of impressions were lost to budget on every day checked; 41-77% were lost to ad rank. Raised the target cost per conversion from $5 to $8.
Sept 13: Caught that Meta's Purchase event has been registering nothing account-wide since at least Aug 25 and corrected the earlier record that reported Meta attribution as fixed and verified.

Sept 11: Found and fixed the GA4 double-count. Two Google Analytics tags in the server-side container were both forwarding every event, dating to a contractor publish on July 31. Every visit was being recorded twice and more than half of purchases were being recorded as two purchases.
Sept 13: Added campaign tags to every Google Ads campaign so Shopify can split branded from non-branded revenue on its own, instead of hand-reconciling three systems.

Sept 13: Turned off the theme's white page-transition overlay and the Smile Guard pop-ups. On a slow phone connection, content now appears at about 3 seconds instead of 9.5, and on Smile Guard instead of 20.7.
Sept 11: Ran live test purchases through both a paid and an organic social path to prove the order-source chain end to end.
Shipped Smile Guard and Cat Probonix as reusable Shopify theme templates, plus a written protocol so this repeats for any Humarian product.
Overhauled the weekly reporting into Meta bar charts with an active-ads breakdown and a written pulse narrative.

ledger.title: GA4 double-count fixed
ledger.detail: Two live GA4 tags in the server container were both forwarding every event since a July 31 contractor publish. The duplicate was paused Sept 11 (server GTM v11). Sessions and purchase counts before that date are inflated and should not be compared directly against figures after it.

ledger.title: Google Ads campaign tagging
ledger.detail: All campaigns now pass a campaign tag through to the site, so Shopify can report branded versus non-branded revenue without manual reconciliation. Verified live on both the settings and the reporting side.

ledger.title: Non-branded Google rebuild
ledger.detail: Root cause was zero-search-volume keywords letting Google's close-variant matching spend the budget on competitor brands. Rebuilt on exact match with 82 negatives. Held paused so the pet campaign gives a clean read first.

ledger.title: Pet symptom campaign live
ledger.detail: $10/day, exact match on cat and dog symptom searches, launched Sept 13. Kill rule agreed up front: $150 spent or 30 days, judged on Shopify orders rather than GA4.

ledger.title: Meta Purchase event returning zero
ledger.detail: Website purchases, purchase value and omni purchases all null every day from Aug 25 through Sept 13, while impressions and spend are normal. Next step is a Meta Events Manager check on the Purchase event to see whether events are arriving at all and whether a deduplication setting is suppressing them.

ledger.title: Server-side purchase feed
ledger.detail: Roughly a quarter of weekly orders complete on Recharge and Checkout Champ, which the web pixel never sees. A webhook feed is the remaining build for true purchase attribution.

ledger.title: Organic social measurement
ledger.detail: Facebook Page Insights and Instagram Insights are not connected to the reporting tool, so organic impressions and reach cannot be pulled. Connecting them is queued.

ledger.title: Pet content as a landing page
ledger.detail: The cat and dog vomiting post already ranks position 3-4. Adding clear conversion links makes it testable as an ad landing page against the product pages for symptom traffic.

ledger.title: Store-wide Judge.me roll-up
ledger.detail: Product-level rating shows on landing pages; no connector exists for the store-wide aggregate. Tracked as a capability gap.
